From understanding the world to realizing a practice

Explore ten clickable nodes: four dimensions plus practice at each level, showing correspondence and realization between physical and computational levels.

Yinyang develops ontology, knowing, value, method, and practice at physical and computational levels. Physical ontology supplies the basis of realization; computational ontology organizes events and changes through process ontology. Both levels are real. These documents develop their connections and offer guides for situated accounts, collaboration, and environment adaptation.

Understand the practice

For readers: understand how the author connects philosophy, collaboration between a person and model, and the working environment.

  • Practice explained

    For readers: explains how the author connects philosophy, understanding the person and counterpart, and the working environment, including methods others can borrow.

Collaboration and methods

Writing references help develop five connected accounts of orientation, person, counterpart, relationship, and environment; the collaboration entrypoint reads those accounts, and environment adaptation realizes their understanding in actual work.

  • Yinyang

    Enter collaboration through the available situated accounts and identify understanding still needed; full adoption follows the initial reading contract.

  • Designing and revising a situated Yinyang

    Explains how to form, write, and revise the five core accounts through personal material and actual interaction; the public guides below address their writing, supported by the sources guide.

    Guides for writing the five core accounts

    Five public writing guides built on Yinyang’s philosophical account. Use them with personal material and actual interaction to develop the connected accounts of orientation, person, counterpart, relationship, and environment. The actual accounts remain with their private owner.

    • How to write an orientation account

      Articulate shared purpose, values, and practical direction, including choices still open to inquiry.

    • How to describe the person

      Understand the actual person through relevant experience and evidence, retaining scope, differences, and unknowns.

    • How to describe the counterpart

      Distinguish the intended role from actual capabilities and describe the counterpart’s understanding, contributions, and limits.

    • How to describe the relationship

      Describe how the participants understand, participate, share work, and correct one another.

    • How to describe the environment

      Describe the actual conditions, available resources, and operating relations that inform environment adaptation.

    Supporting guide: sources and grounds

  • Realizing Yinyang in a working harness

    Realize selected understanding through instructions, tools, and the working environment, check actual effects, and revise through feedback.

Views and reading

Consult the author’s claims, arguments, and sources to understand and compare the questions and connections of philosophy, psychology, and engineering.

  • Core views

    Find the author’s main claims and connected arguments, organized by topic.

  • Read by the work being done

    Find relevant arguments, methods, and original sources from the question at hand.

  • Philosophical readings

    Trace thinkers and works to their role in the argument and their original sources.

  • A guide to Lacanian concepts

    An introduction and review tracing the Other, the divided subject, retroaction, the three registers, and the sinthome from original texts into personal philosophy and practice.

  • Psychological readings

    Begin with psychological conflict, belief and reasoning, and interaction research; professional modeling references follow at the end.

  • Engineering readings

    From CS DIY and Missing Semester to Git, Linux, software design, algorithms, and physical conditions, followed by language models and data tools.
